The first riser nominal profile is distinct from the bottom trim that compensates for the tread/floor finish. SVG uses nominal step vertices and is NOT a 1:1 saw template or actual stock outline. Actual top/bottom bearing, nosing, throat code limits, fasteners, total stock, fit and structural safety require site verification. Nosing and optional upper landing are drawn as distinct reference overlays, not actual saw cut geometry, support details, board stock length or a guaranteed stock purchasing length. Enter a nosing projection smaller than the horizontal tread run. Coordinate datums refer to the nominal notch profile, not measured finished tread overhang or construction approval. The calculated notched section and parallel lower stock edge are a mathematical side-view MODEL, not a verified original rectangular blank, complete physical cut outline or structural timber specification. Their vertical end-closing edges are reference clips at the first and last riser x coordinates, NOT safe bearing cut positions. Lower and upper support run inputs represent measured horizontal surface references only: they do not determine contact, end cuts, bolts, landings or bearing adequacy. No purchase board length or 1:1 template is inferred. Use independent field verification and professional structural review for actual end bearing. All riser/tread sawline segments are nominal coordinates. Optional end cut offsets are separately user-chosen intersections on the mathematical stock lower edge, not actual approved bearing cuts. A longitudinal stock-fit check is a mathematical bound only and never structural verification.

guidance.heading: Separate the two diagonals
guidance.text: The nominal notch pitch line runs from the top of the first riser to the top landing, with rise equal to the 13 inter-riser steps. The floor-to-floor chord starts at the lower datum and has a different angle and length. Neither should automatically be ordered or cut as a raw timber board length.

guidance.heading: Review the exact nominal step-coordinate diagram
guidance.text: The SVG now draws from the same (x,height) vertices generated by the engine: 14 riser segments, with 13 horizontal tread segments. The diagram's dashed pitch reference and floor chord are distinct. It is a scaled schematic, not a physical full-size pattern.

guidance.heading: Correct the bottom cut for installed finishes
guidance.text: For conventional tread installation, bottom layout cut height = one nominal riser − finished tread thickness + any lower finish installed after the stringer. This is an end-trim reference only; it does not shift all nominal riser elevations. The diagram marks that bottom reference independently.

guidance.heading: Nominal throat is not an engineering rating
guidance.text: Stock normal depth less step notch penetration gives a nominal remaining throat. Capacity depends on wood grade, defects, fasteners, local code and actual support details; do not treat the geometric clearance or illustrated diagonal as engineered approval.

guidance.heading: Separate nosing references from actual stringer saw cuts
guidance.text: Enter a nonnegative optional horizontal tread nose projection smaller than the repeated tread run. Its marker projects toward the lower level from each nominal riser line (including a negative coordinate at the first tread nose). The nominal step cutline remains unchanged: this reference does not add timber to the stringer or certify the correct nosing design.

guidance.heading: Show upper landing reach without inflating notch length
guidance.text: If you have a separate top landing depth measurement, enter its optional horizontal extension. The worksheet shows its start at the final riser x coordinate and its end at the nominal flight run plus the extension. This is NOT a longer stringer notch pitch line, physical board cut length, engineered top connection or extra counted tread.

guidance.heading: Read the colored section as a modeled profile, not a raw stock cut template
guidance.text: The shaded polygon follows the repeated saw-tooth notch references and a mathematically parallel lower edge separated from the upper pitch line by the entered nominal board depth. The lower boundary and the vertical closing edges at the first and last risers are idealized reference boundaries; physical bearing cuts, end trim, ledger connection, full raw board dimensions, knots and real stock face defects are NOT supplied. The computed face area is a side-section geometry check, not a lumber purchase or strength rating.

guidance.heading: Check the minimum remaining wood depth using a perpendicular throat
guidance.text: The deepest modeled notch corners all lie one riser below the upper pitch line. Convert that drop into a distance perpendicular to the stringer pitch, then subtract from the user-entered normal stock depth. For 7.5 in rise per 10 in tread and 11.25 in normal depth, penetration is 6 in and nominal minimum throat 5.25 in. The tool rejects a nonpositive remaining throat; positive alone does not establish structural suitability or compliance.

guidance.heading: Lower and upper support surfaces are independent site measurements
guidance.text: Optional lower and upper horizontal support surface runs appear as separately styled reference segments at the bottom and top finished-level datums, outside the nominal stringer cut span. They are not cut faces and they do not imply the stringer physically sits on either segment. Actual end-bearing shape, clearance, fastening, attachment strength and local building-code checks require measured framing details and professional review.

guidance.heading: Use exact nominal riser/tread sawlines, not merely a zigzag sketch
guidance.text: The extra sawline table contains one line for every actual nominal vertical riser and horizontal tread leg. Both endpoints, length and angle are calculated from the same stepVertices that drive the green SVG profile. The numeric CSV converts every X/Y and segment length to the selected unit. Saw kerf, saw blade overcuts and workshop tolerances are not included.

guidance.heading: Optional user-measured end-line intersection references
guidance.text: Enter nonnegative lower and upper horizontal extensions locating the chosen intersection of an end line with the existing parallel lower reference edge. A positive measured extension creates an explicit orange end line from the bottom/top nominal notch corner to that geometric intersection. These are user-chosen points, independent from the optional SUPPORT SURFACE lengths, and are not automatically safe bearing cuts. Check actual ledger/stringer connection, end angles and real raw material before cutting.

guidance.heading: Read the stock-axis envelope as a geometric bound only
guidance.text: The calculator projects the nominal 2D sawtooth and chosen end points onto the stair pitch direction and adds your per-end stock allowance. A measured board length can be compared to this modeled longitudinal envelope, but width, support cuts, knots, slope-aligned blank positioning, material defects and certified usable stock cannot be inferred. A pass is not construction approval.

tools.title: Roof Sheathing Calculator
tools.desc: Rectangular single-slope roof sheathing grid with complete sheet start/end cuts, per-sheet scrap and independent stock-area conservation

options.label: Conservative: one fresh sheet per installed cut
Try nonrotated stock bounding-box reuse (bounded heuristic)

tools.formula: True sloped uphill length = plan width×sqrt(1+(pitch/12)²). Grid sheet positions from the eave origin in stock face coordinates; for each position, cut end = min(sheet boundary, roof edge) on BOTH axes. Each consumed stock sheet area = used cut area+discarded offcut area, even if fully uncut. Total sheet stock area = used roof area+sum of all discarded offcuts; any purchasing allowance is applied separately to whole sheet count.
tools.example: Flat 110×70 in roof surface, 96×48 in stock oriented with 96 in along eave: four sheet positions cut to 96×48, 14×48, 96×22 and 14×22 in. 7,700 in² roof area + 10,732 in² discarded stock offcuts = 18,432 in² from four stock sheets. This is a one-sheet-per-position reference, not a reusable offcut nesting plan.
tools.limit: One rectangular roof plane with flat developed sloped-surface coordinates; sheet start/end coordinates, cut dimensions and scrap areas are geometry-only. Each occupied cut position consumes one NEW full stock sheet, even when a real offcut might be reused. No overlap allowance, seam joints, rafter bearing, fastening, panel expansion gaps, bracing, strength or building-code approvals are modelled. Very small edge remnants and exact real saw tolerances require review. SVG is not an actual 1:1 cutting template. Optional reuse is a bounded no-rotation rectangular BOUNDING-BOX heuristic for at most 400 pieces; all polygon corner scrap is treated as inaccessible. User-entered split-line kerf does not cover actual angled polygon perimeter cutting, safe blade clearance, support framing, fastening, or expansion gaps. Validate physical saw cuts and install before purchase.

guidance.heading: Read the roof axes and every cut boundary
guidance.text: The roof plan width is the horizontal uphill run and the plan length follows the eave. The uphill distance is converted to its developed sloped length before laying the sheet grid. Each CSV row includes grid row and column, both eave start/end and uphill start/end coordinates, and the resulting stock cut dimensions.

guidance.heading: Audit stock and scrap independently
guidance.text: For each occupied position, one whole stock sheet is consumed. The used cut rectangle plus its unreused stock offcut area must equal the original sheet area. The sum of used rectangles covers the developed roof area and the sum of offcuts is reported explicitly. Switching the stock orientation may change this per-sheet waste without changing the roof geometry.

guidance.heading: No nesting, waste reuse or engineered fastener layout
guidance.text: Cut-off remnants from one sheet are deliberately NOT assigned to another position. The order count applies your separate waste allowance to the number of occupied positions. Verify any real seam support, panel fasteners, manufacturer instructions, material expansion and safe roof construction outside this trial-only geometry.

guidance.heading: Optional stock offcut assignment is geometrically explicit
guidance.text: An optional bounded layout packs every finished cut's axis-aligned bounding box onto supplier-size sheets, using deterministic nonrotated guillotine splits. Every stock placement exports its own X/Y and polygon vertices relative to the original stock face, with a separate split-line kerf. Used polygon area, inaccessible scrap inside boxes, lost kerf and remaining free stock must equal purchased stock area. This is a feasible geometric arrangement within the chosen assumptions, NOT an optimal layout, bearing approval or verified saw path.

tools.title: Fence Post Layout Calculator
tools.desc: End-center-to-end-center fence post layout with physical left/right post faces, true outside length and clear-bay conservation
tools.formula: Bays = ceil(end-center distance/maximum OC); actual OC = end-center distance/bays; clear bay = actual OC−post face width. Outside-to-outside length = center span+one full post face width; (bays+1) post faces + bays clear bays = outside length.
tools.example: 1200 in between end post centers at maximum 96 in OC uses 13 bays, 14 posts and 92.3077 in actual center spacing. With 3.5-in faces, each clear bay is 88.8077 in; total outside-to-outside span is 1203.5 in.
tools.limit: Length is between END POST CENTERS, not outside-to-outside fence length. The first face extends half a post width BEFORE center coordinate zero, and the last extends half a width beyond the final center. The diagram spans outer post faces, while ticks mark the entered center references. Actual posts, lateral load, footing, slope, rails, gate frames, hardware and codes are excluded; geometric spacing is NOT construction approval.

guidance.heading: Start and end at post centers
guidance.text: Enter the measured distance between the first and last post center. The physical post faces occupy coordinates center±half the actual face width. Outside-to-outside length is consequently one post width greater than the center run.

guidance.heading: Check clear bay and full post-face conservation
guidance.text: The tool equally divides the center run into a whole number of bays at or below the maximum entered OC spacing. Every gap between adjacent post faces is the OC interval less one full post width. Posts cannot touch or overlap. The sum of all faces and all clear bays must equal the outside total length.

guidance.heading: The drawing is the whole physical outside span
guidance.text: The SVG now maps every actual post face within an outside-to-outside reference frame, rather than drawing half of the first and last posts beyond the diagram bounds. The CSV retains signed end-face coordinates because center zero is the datum. Field installation and structural design are separate.
